item.title: CISA orders agencies to patch and replace end-of-life devices, citing active exploitation
item.description: The directive gives agencies three months to identify unsupported edge devices, a year to begin removing them and 18 months to eliminate them entirely.

item.title: Super Bowl gears up for massive security operation
item.description: While immigration officials will reportedly not be present at the San Francisco game this weekend, a raft of federal, state and local agencies will be on site to keep the event safe from various threats.

item.title: Social Security is directing employees who normally process benefits to answer phones instead
item.description: After shedding thousands of employees, SSA is reassigning workers amid fears the moves will cause backlogs to grow.

item.title: Now accepting applications — for classified intel
item.description: Foreign adversaries are using fake jobs and consulting gigs to coax secrets from former U.S. officials. It’s had results, and the efforts don’t appear to be slowing.

item.title: VA’s latest AI inventory includes new suicide, EHR-focused use cases
item.description: Seventy-two of the AI use cases previously included in the department’s 2024 inventory were listed as retired, meaning that their “development and/or use has since been discontinued.”

item.title: Tech bills of the week: Restricting biometric use; expanding the quantum workforce; and more
item.description: Congress avoided a second mini-shutdown and saw a return-to-normal influx of new tech bills.

item.title: Gabbard’s office denies wrongdoing amid scrutiny over whistleblower complaint
item.description: ODNI said she acted within her authority in response to reports describing an NSA-intercepted phone call tied to the case.

item.title: CIA announces new acquisition framework to speed tech adoption
item.description: DARPA alum Efstathia Fragogiannis joined the agency as its new procurement chief in November and will be spearheading the effort, according to a CIA official.

item.title: Gabbard’s expanded role in election security draws scrutiny
item.description: Since the start of the year, the White House chief of staff and DHS secretary have met multiple times to discuss election security, and DNI Tulsi Gabbard has been present in at least one of those meetings, according to a U.S. official.

item.title: Navigating FedRAMP 20x and the continuous compliance imperative
item.description: COMMENTARY | FedRAMP 20x is a great step forward, but there is still work to be done.
